content.user_title: Improve Tests by Avoiding Mock Anti-Patterns
content.value_statement: Poor tests often verify mocks instead of real application behavior. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a checklist for safer TDD, focused mocks, and cleaner test design.
actual_capabilities: Identifies tests that assert on mock existence instead of real behavior.
Warns against adding test-only methods to production classes.
Guides users to understand side effects before introducing mocks.
Encourages complete mock data that mirrors real API responses.
Promotes TDD as a way to avoid late or shallow tests.
limitations: Does not run tests or inspect runtime behavior by itself.
Does not replace project-specific testing standards or framework documentation.
Examples focus on TypeScript-style tests, though the concepts are broader.
Requires the user or agent to verify real dependencies and API shapes.

use_cases.title: Review a new unit test
use_cases.description: Check whether a test proves product behavior or only checks that a mock was rendered.

use_cases.title: Plan test cleanup during refactoring
use_cases.description: Move cleanup helpers out of production classes and into test utilities where appropriate.

use_cases.title: Set testing standards for contributors
use_cases.description: Give reviewers a shared checklist for mocking decisions, TDD flow, and integration test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Check one test for mock assertions
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small test change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing anti-patterns skill to review this test. Tell me if it verifies real behavior or only verifies a mock.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a mock-heavy test
prompt_templates.scenario: Refactor a brittle test with too much setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this test with the testing anti-patterns skill. Suggest the smallest change that reduces mocking while preserving useful isolation.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate production code added for tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Check whether a method belongs in production code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing anti-patterns skill to inspect this production method and its tests. Decide whether the method is test-only and should move to test utilities.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a testing strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a feature branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the testing anti-patterns skill across this feature branch. Identify mock behavior tests, incomplete mocks, missing integration coverage, and places where TDD would improve confidence.

output_examples.input: A test asserts that sidebar-mock is present after rendering a page.
output_examples.output: The test verifies the mock, not the page behavior. Prefer rendering the real sidebar or asserting on navigation behavior visible to users.

output_examples.input: A Session class gets a destroy method only so tests can clean up workspaces.
output_examples.output: This is production pollution for a test need. Move cleanup into a test utility unless Session owns that lifecycle in production.

output_examples.input: A duplicate detection test mocks the method that writes configuration state.
output_examples.output: The mock removes a side effect the test depends on. Mock a lower-level slow dependency or run the real method first to confirm required behavior.

best_practices: Write or inspect the failing test before adding mocks.
Mock the smallest external or slow boundary that preserves required behavior.
Keep production APIs focused on production lifecycle responsibilities.
anti_patterns: Asserting that mock elements or fake test IDs exist.
Adding production methods that are only called by tests.
Creating partial mock responses without checking the real response shape.

faq.question: Does this skill ban mocks?
faq.answer: No. It encourages mocks only when they isolate a real boundary without replacing behavior the test must verify.

faq.question: Can I still use unit tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill helps unit tests stay focused on observable behavior instead of mock implementation details.

faq.question: When should I choose an integration test?
faq.answer: Use an integration test when mocks become more complex than the behavior being tested or hide important side effects.

faq.question: How does this relate to TDD?
faq.answer: TDD helps expose real behavior before mocks are introduced, reducing tests that pass for the wrong reason.

faq.question: Does this skill run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance. You still need to run tests and inspect failures in your project.

faq.question: Is this only for TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: No. The examples use TypeScript, but the testing principles apply to many languages and frameworks.
